sectors.trend: Iron ore faces a structural shakeout as demand softens, though war premium temporarily masks weakness. Gold and critical-minerals small caps (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) show relative strength.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore consolidation. Gold miners (NVA.AX, GSG.AX) and critical-minerals names benefit from energy-transition demand. War premium is a false signal for iron ore.

sectors.trend: RBA unlikely to cut rates to support property; housing construction declining. ASIC scrutiny of Big Four raises systemic risk. Victoria's debt warning pressures state-linked credit.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face rising NPL risk from property and construction. ASIC review (headline 67) could pressure audit-firm clients. Rate-sensitive REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) under pressure.

sectors.trend: EV adoption accelerates (BYD tipping point, EVs outpace petrol). Sydney CBD solar farm and clean-power investment theme gaining traction. El Niño cyclone risk adds energy infrastructure urgency.
sectors.implications: Wesfarmers (WES.AX) and Coles (COL.AX) face fuel-margin pressure. Clean-energy and grid names (e.g., AGL.AX, CGP.AX) benefit. EV supply-chain exposure via BYD (not ASX-listed) shifts consumer spend.

sectors.trend: Household sentiment weak ('Australians feel poorer'); unpaid-work burden and cost-of-living pressure persist. EV switch reduces fuel spend but adds charging infrastructure costs. Cigarette tax debate may boost tobacco revenue.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, CSL.AX (defensive) relatively resilient. Tobacco tax fight (headline 45) could support BAT/PM revenue but is politically contentious. CSL.AX benefits from global oncology M&A (McKesson $2.25B buy, headline 8).

sectors.trend: Global AI momentum (Salesforce, Nvidia, Okta +20%, Apple on-device AI) continues but ASX tech exposure is thin. Australia faces AI-worker and tradie shortages; skilled migration prioritised.
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX tech plays; indirect benefit to BHP.AX, CSL.AX via AI-driven efficiency. Skilled-migration policy (headline 52) supports labour-intensive sectors. Defence drone disruption (headline 46) relevant to ASX defence names.

key_themes: RBA on hold / higher-for-longer rates pressuring property and rate-sensitive sectors
Iron ore structural shakeout vs. temporary war premium
ASIC regulatory scrutiny of Big Four accountants
Small-cap mining and critical minerals outperforming large caps
Household affordability crisis and weak per-capita growth

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate path / property market stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to rate-sensitive REITs and property developers; favour dividend-paying large-cap banks with strong capital buffers.
Diversify materials exposure toward gold, copper, and critical minerals; avoid over-concentration in iron ore (BHP.AX, FMG.AX).
Screen ASX construction and infrastructure names for balance-sheet stress; monitor Worksafe and ASIC enforcement actions.
Maintain gold and energy hedges; monitor oil and LNG pricing for WES.AX and energy names.
Monitor ratings agency actions; reduce exposure to Victorian REITs and state-linked infrastructure.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Niño / cyclone risk to infrastructure
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review insurance and infrastructure exposure; monitor Qld-based energy and resources assets.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical-minerals small caps
opportunities.rationale: Gold discovery (Aurum) and critical-minerals momentum (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) offer upside in a rate-uncertain environment; energy-transition demand structural.

opportunities.recommendation: Add defensive large-cap healthcare and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: Weak household sentiment and 'Australians feel poorer' narrative supports defensive positioning; CSL.AX benefits from global oncology M&A wave.
EV tipping point confirmed by BYD; Sydney CBD solar farm and El Niño-driven infrastructure urgency support long-term clean-power thesis.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore concentration and property/REIT exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore shakeout structural; RBA will not rescue property; housing construction declining. War premium is temporary.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge geopolitical and commodity volatility with gold and energy
defensive_moves.rationale: Iran-US tensions unresolved; Trump 'mission accomplished' declaration may be premature. Gold and LNG provide natural hedges.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Monitor construction and audit-firm regulatory risk
defensive_moves.rationale: Bathla collapse, Worksafe/Star, and ASIC Big Four review signal potential contagion in construction and professional-services sectors.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower over 1–3 months. Higher-for-longer RBA rates, iron ore softness, and property construction decline weigh on sentiment. Geopolitical headlines (Iran) add volatility. Small-cap miners and gold provide relative outperformance. 'Bull case returns' (headline 68) is a contrarian signal but not yet confirmed by breadth.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pivots on inflation data. Structural themes: EV transition, critical-minerals demand, AI-driven productivity, and energy infrastructure capex. Key risk: construction-sector contagion and weak per-capita growth (Australia vs Canada). Iron ore shakeout may create consolidation opportunities for well-capitalised miners.
